Labors from Division 2 of Special Vehicles Section 2, Security Bureau, Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department, were deployed to help rescue people from the fire at the Iberis Tower Building in Sakura Ward, Miyato City, Miyato Prefecture.
The unit was transported to the roof by helicopter and carried out rescues using cables. However, possibly because of an operating error, a Labor damaged the building, sending debris falling to the ground.
Fortunately, nobody was injured, but nearby residents have voiced concerns about the Labor unit.

The major mobile phone company Lightning Connect recently made headlines over a massive customer-data leak. Apparently, it began when an attacker inferred a password from words spoken by a sales employee on a mobile phone in another company's elevator, then broke into its computer system.

entries.en:
Around 9 p.m. today, a man with a mohawk chased a couple while shouting loudly on the observation-deck floor of the Iberis Tower Building, which later caught fire.
The fire had begun before Miyato Prefectural Police arrived in response to the report. The matter remains under investigation, and no solid information was available.
Witnesses described the pursuer as 'a tall, dark-complexioned man in a suit with a mohawk.' Any connection with the fire is unknown.

entries.en:
Around 9:30 p.m. today, a report was received of two people carrying handguns on an office floor of the Iberis Tower Building.
Before this, 'a tall, dark-complexioned man in a suit with a mohawk' had chased a couple on the observation-deck floor. Miyato Prefectural Police are investigating on the assumption that the same person was involved.
T, who made the report, said, 'They suddenly came into the room shouting loudly and seemed to be looking for someone. I couldn't really tell what their hair was like.' Any connection with the fire is unknown.

entries.en:

entries.en:
It rarely comes up in conversation, but do you know how long an answering machine records? Twenty seconds? Thirty? You would need about that long to leave a message. Yet Mossy, the latest landline phone from industry leader Irodori Electric, offers an astonishing five seconds! Isn't that rather short? We decided to ask why.
Us: 'Hello. Why does Mossy record for only five seconds?'
Irodori: 'Well, when we averaged the recorded messages on all the landline phones we've sold, it came to 2.5 seconds. We figured twice that would be enough, so we made it five.'
Us: 'What!? 2.5 seconds? Could you even say hello in that time?'
Irodori: 'Our own investigation confirmed an average of 2.5 seconds. For privacy reasons, we measured only the duration, not the content.'
Us: 'D-doesn't that include calls where people hung up without leaving a message...?'
To be continued next issue.

entries.en:
Before dawn today, a fire broke out at the Iberis Tower Building in Sakura Ward, Miyato City, Miyato Prefecture. Floors fourteen through twenty-five were damaged, and the fire is believed to have originated in the twentieth-floor offices.
Miyato Prefectural Police found no incendiary material, but traces of extreme force around the origin suggest something like an explosive was responsible.
According to building staff, several people had seen an unaffiliated man walking around the twentieth floor over the past few days. Investigators are continuing their work on the possibility that he planted explosives.

entries.en:
Dr. Fukazawa, leader of the survey team aboard the research vessel Shibazakura, earned her doctorate overseas at a young age and was regarded internationally as a promising marine life researcher.
Her paper published three years ago, 'The Relationship Between Pulse Rate and Lifespan in Giant Creatures Inhabiting the Seabed,' was selected as the best paper of its time by Poseidon Neptune, the most authoritative journal in marine biology.
News of Dr. Fukazawa's death has brought expressions of grief from marine researchers around the world.

entries.en:
Ebine Publishing, headquartered in Hananira Town, Miyato City, suffered major damage to its building from the giant alien that appeared there today. Amid this, it has welcomed a new owner and is aiming to recover. Employee Mukojima said, 'Much of the roof has collapsed, and we don't know where our other colleagues are. Honestly, I thought it was all over. But the new owner said they want to revive Ebine Publishing. I intend to do everything I can to live up to that.'
However, Ebine Publishing faces an extremely difficult road. Not only its building but the surrounding roads are badly damaged, making normal work impossible. It seems questionable whether it needs to remain attached to this building. Its next moves will attract attention.

entries.en:
Ebine Publishing, publisher of Giant Shadow Weekly, announced that it will sell its entire business, land, and building. This week's issue will be the magazine's last. The main cause is believed to be the extensive damage from the giant alien that appeared today in Hananira Town, where its building stands.
Employee Mukojima said, 'The roof is badly damaged, and our other colleagues are missing. I didn't think we could keep going. Hearing that the magazine was closing, I thought, just as I feared. I have no idea what to do from tomorrow.'
Ebine Publishing had changed owners shortly before this. The sale is said to have earned that owner at least two billion yen.
